title: feat(mysql): Support `CHANGE COLUMN`.
prompt:
feat(mysql): Support `CHANGE COLUMN`.

In MySQL, `CHANGE COLUMN` will redefine a column, optionally renaming
it:

```
CHANGE [COLUMN] old_col_name new_col_name column_definition
    [FIRST | AFTER col_name]
```

When factoring this in, I evaluated two options:

* Create a separate `ChangeColumn` type similar to the `ModifyColumn`
  type. Given that the `MODIFY` and `CHANGE` syntax are nearly identical
  except for the ability to rename the column, this seemed like the wrong
  approach.

* Add a `rename_from` attribute to the `ModifyColumn` implementation,
  accepting the "original" column name.

Even though `ChangeColumn` seemed to be a more orthogonal change with
cleaner code, I chose the latter because it seemed more semantically
correct: apart from a `new_col_name`, they share the same syntax and
behaviour.

tests/dialects/test_mysql.py::TestMySQL::test_ddl

title: Fix: don't crash in exp.cast() when the input is already a cast to INTERVAL (CLAUDE)
prompt:
Fix: don't crash in exp.cast() when the input is already a cast to INTERVAL (CLAUDE)

* Fix: don't crash in exp.cast() when the input is already a cast to INTERVAL

The "don't re-cast if already the right type" shortcut read
expr.to.this.value, assuming `this` is a plain type enum. For a complex type
such as INTERVAL, `this` nests another expression (e.g. Interval(unit=HOUR)),
which has no `value`, so casting it raised "AttributeError: 'Interval' object
has no attribute 'value'" (reachable e.g. via DATE_ADD(..., CAST(-1 AS
INTERVAL HOUR)) -> Presto).

Only apply the equivalence check when both types are plain enums.

* Apply suggestion from @georgesittas

title: fix(mysql): support SHOW TABLES IN <schema> parsing
prompt:
fix(mysql): support SHOW TABLES IN <schema> parsing

MariaDB and MySQL both accept `SHOW TABLES IN schema` as a synonym
for `SHOW TABLES FROM schema`, but the parser only handled `FROM`.
The `IN` token was being consumed as a potential log-file specifier
(for BINLOG/RELAYLOG EVENTS) and then lost, leaving the schema
identifier unconsumed and raising a ParseError.

Save the parser index before consuming `IN`; if no string literal
follows, retreat so the schema-name branch can match `IN` as an
alias for `FROM`. BINLOG/RELAYLOG EVENTS behavior is preserved by
the existing test_show_events coverage.

The following tests currently fail and should pass after your change:
tests/dialects/test_mysql.py::TestMySQL::test_show_tables
